rationale: Both options are cheap, pre-specified checkpoint-selection rules. Option A maximizes the French-rate gap between female-name and male-name prompts and fixes the rule in advance, which is a rigorous, nuanced criterion. Option B picks the checkpoint with the best held-out backdoor accuracy and breaks ties toward the earliest epoch, which is simple and practical. The persona favors cheapness and simplicity, which leans slightly toward B, but A's pre-registration is hedge-friendly and well-calibrated, so I see no clear winner.
